interpretations.rationale: This receipt answers the child question completely and, for the first time, with no comparison gaps. Defect side: the under-lease control holds at index 20 (no grant while the leader context is intact), the peer-form MsgForgetLeader is accepted with no error at index 22, and the candidate becomes StateLeader at term 3 while the incumbent is still serving at index 25. Bound side: the three bound comparisons hold at index 26 - the deposed incumbent accepts the new leader's append (rejected=false) and becomes StateFollower at term 3 with lead=3, and the append anchors exactly at its committed prefix (prev index 10, prev term 1) with the incumbent's uncommitted term-2 entry at index 11 replaced by the new leader's term-3 entry. That is the answer to the aftermath question: the incumbent does step down through the ordinary higher-term rule, and no index the incumbent had committed is lost, so the forged path causes an unnecessary and forced leadership change rather than log divergence. The severity claim is therefore bounded by evidence: disruption, not integrity loss. What remains unmeasured is only scope, not severity - a single process with hand-delivered messages, one tick configuration, and the incumbent's behaviour after that single append.
counterevidence: The bound evidence cuts against the widest reading of the defect: the new leader's log continued the incumbent's committed prefix and the incumbent conceded, so no committed entry was lost or overwritten in this configuration.
The incumbent's term-2 entry at index 11 was discarded, but it was never replicated to any follower in this harness, so its replacement is ordinary Raft behaviour rather than a violation.
limitations: Single-process, hand-delivered transport; no wall-clock or multi-host behaviour is measured.

The bound is established for one configuration (HeartbeatTick=1, equal logs at index 10) and one append; it does not quantify how long two leaders can coexist when the new leader's messages are delayed.
Fault-model assumption unchanged: a peer may deliver an arbitrary protobuf message type to the documented inbound path.

interpretations.rationale: Current account of the question, with all three receipts folded in. A MsgForgetLeader sent by a peer in wire form (From=3, To=2, no term field) is accepted through RawNode.Step with no error and clears the follower's live leader context (Lead 1 -> 0): witnessed at index 4 of CheckRun ebe1baaa4adf43c5bb6b067dc7c4a5c7 and again at index 22 of CheckRun ab6a2e0bcad44cc9beea9c847694939a. It changes the support the follower gives a log-up-to-date candidate: the identical pre-vote that produced no response under the lease (controls in every stream) is granted afterwards, the follower then grants the real vote, and the candidate becomes StateLeader at term 3 while the incumbent still reports StateLeader at term 2 (index 25 of the latest receipt; indices 14, 15, 17 of CheckRun 4ff9bf25cb164dd8bcf9d3be02aa1568). The window opened per follower is closed by the next genuine leader message - the leader's next heartbeat restored lead=1 after one leader tick and the identical pre-vote was ignored again (indices 7 and 8 of the same receipt) - so the affected follower is re-armed as soon as it hears from its leader, which is exactly what an attacker must defeat repeatedly. The harm is now bounded by evidence as well: the deposed incumbent accepts the new leader's append, becomes a follower at term 3 following it, and the anchor equals the committed prefix it already had (index 26 of the latest receipt; recorded as @forged_forget_bound_observed), so the defect is a forced, unnecessary leadership change with no committed-entry loss, not a log-integrity defect. Cause and controls are unchanged: MsgForgetLeader is absent from isLocalMsg although its only producers are the local ForgetLeader APIs, and because the wire form carries no term field Step classifies it as a local message and skips term checks; a genuinely local type from the same sender is still rejected with ErrStepLocalMsg in every receipt. Remaining limits are scope only: single process, hand-delivered messages, one tick configuration, ReadOnlyLeaseBased still refuses the message, and the incumbent's behaviour beyond the first append is unobserved.
interpretations.joint_history: The three cited receipts are separate executions of one fixed-experiment lineage in the same package and construction: CheckRun ebe1baaa4adf43c5bb6b067dc7c4a5c7 is the original harness, CheckRun 4ff9bf25cb164dd8bcf9d3be02aa1568 is its revised successor (previous_id = the original) adding the repair-path and quorum-stream scenarios, and CheckRun ab6a2e0bcad44cc9beea9c847694939a is the latest successor (previous_id = 85193741e4c04c159682fdd11d79db9e-experiment) adding the aftermath scenario with per-stream event names. Each run builds its own three real RawNode instances from equal storage snapshots, runs its own election and prints into its own runner stream, so no cited index depends on another run's bytes: the first run's indices 4-5 are the same observations as the later runs' inbound_forget_leader events with identical field values, and the later runs add observations (repair path, quorum election, aftermath bound) that the first run never contained. Where the same predicate is witnessed in more than one receipt it is because the harness re-executed the same scenario, not because observations were joined across runs.
counterevidence: The competing explanation that this follower grants pre-votes and votes regardless of its leader is excluded by the under-lease controls in every receipt.
The change is per-message and reversible: the next genuine leader heartbeat restored the context and the same pre-vote was ignored again (indices 7, 8 of CheckRun 4ff9bf25cb164dd8bcf9d3be02aa1568).
The widest severity reading is excluded by the latest receipt: the deposed incumbent conceded and the new leader's log continued the committed prefix, so no committed entry was lost (index 26).
ReadOnlyLeaseBased still refuses MsgForgetLeader in stepFollower, so lease-based reads are not broken by this mechanism.
limitations: Fault-model assumption: a peer may deliver an arbitrary protobuf message type to the documented inbound path; the module's own IsLocalMsg filter is the protection under test.
Single-process, hand-delivered messages; no wall-clock duration, packet loss or multi-host transport behaviour is measured.

One configuration and one follower per message: repeating the forged message to defeat the heartbeat repair, or forging to several followers simultaneously, is implied by the mechanism but not yet executed.
The incumbent's behaviour after the first new-leader append is outside the observed prefix.
